reviewer: Codex, interactive AI source review (no paid API call)
summary: Approved as an API reference collection with all 39 scanner warnings assessed. Examples can run paid APIs, deploy infrastructure and log local commands. Some hooks only warn and do not enforce protection. This is not a ready-to-run security boundary or a ChatGPT installation.

warnings.assessment: Documented uv installer from astral.sh; external installer remains outside this source review. Inspect separately before execution.
Same uv installer in the SDK setup guide; optional setup command, not executed in this review.
README describes SRE write-validation hooks. It is descriptive documentation, not a hook invocation.
Reviewer guidance explicitly forbids hardcoded secrets; the match is a negative example.
Audit guidance lists the hardcoded key assignment as an anti-pattern.
Style guide shows a placeholder credential as a bad example.
Evaluation answer text describes AWS credential providers; it does not read local credentials.
Container build installs Node from NodeSource and the Claude CLI. External supply-chain dependencies are not covered by this scan.
Scheduled reviewer builds a PreToolUse denial response. Accepted as an example; not a proof of complete sandboxing.
SRE setup writes validation hooks and infrastructure files. Run only in a disposable demo project; configuration checks are limited.
Chief-of-staff configuration activates local audit hooks. The Edit hook names a missing report-tracker.py123; not reliable audit enforcement.
Local report tracker records file paths, action and word count under audit/. It does not upload records in the inspected code.
Local script logger records full matching commands and descriptions. Commands can contain secrets: do not pass secrets on the command line or publish these logs.
Documentation requests a localhost health endpoint for the demo.
Kubernetes quickstart validates the provided key against api.anthropic.com, then builds a local cluster. Expected credential destination; infrastructure changes require separate review.
Documentation requests a local demo endpoint with an example bearer token.
Observability Dockerfile installs NodeSource packages and the Claude CLI. Container/installer dependencies remain outside this review.
Slack SDK is initialized with the explicitly configured bot token; this integration can send Slack messages when run.
Sentry documentation illustrates blocked exfiltration with a placeholder credential; it explicitly explains residual host permissions.
HTTP MCP server requires a configured bearer token and imports timingSafeEqual. This is server authentication, not an outbound key transfer.
Linear webhook client receives its configured signing secret for validation.
Linear OAuth demo uses its configured client secret and stores tokens in a local JSON file. Protect that file and review production storage separately.
Roadtrip setup checks API credentials before provisioning demo resources; external API usage and costs remain the operator responsibility.
Daytona webhook constructs the Anthropic client with configured environment and webhook credentials.
Upgrade guide passes an environment service key to the Anthropic worker; documentation for deliberate sandbox operation.
Usage guide creates an authenticated Anthropic worker in an explicit workspace.
Modal webhook constructs the Anthropic client with environment and webhook credentials.
Modal runner gives a worker unrestricted paths inside its intended sandbox. Do not run it against a sensitive host filesystem; base URL configuration must be trusted.
Vercel KV client uses its configured URL/token. Protect both environment values; no unrelated destination is shown in this finding.
Vercel runner supplies its configured environment key to the Anthropic client. Sandbox and base URL configuration need independent deployment review.
Slack integration initializes the Slack WebClient with the supplied bot token; external messaging is intentional functionality.
Slack event handler uses the signing secret for HMAC verification with timestamp tolerance.
Agent utility supplies the Anthropic API key to the Anthropic SDK; calls can incur charges.
Skills demo registers three local hooks. These are convenience checks, not a robust enforcement mechanism.
Pre-bash hook prints warnings and exits successfully; it does not block destructive commands.
Pre-write hook prints warnings and exits successfully; it does not prevent overwriting protected files.
Session-start hook checks the environment, imports the installed SDK and creates outputs/. It checks key presence without printing its value.
Notebook test compares source strings to recognize environment-based credential loading; not a secret read itself.
Documented embeddings request sends the configured Voyage key to api.voyageai.com; intentional paid API example.
